output.review_comment:
The fix works around the tests instead of following the docstring. It includes the end date only when `start` and `end` fall in the same month and year. The docstring says nothing like this, business-day counting has no reason to depend on month boundaries, and the PR description calls it "the key insight." That points to logic reverse-engineered from the test cases, not taken from the spec. It also gives inconsistent results: Wed Jan 28 → Mon Feb 2 skips Feb 2, but the same weekday span within one month would count its end date.

If the tests can only pass with a month-dependent rule, they probably conflict with the docstring. The teammate said the docstrings are the source of truth and not to change the tests. So implement exactly what the docstring says (start excluded, end included if it's a business day, holidays excluded, negative and antisymmetric when `end < start`). Then report any tests that still fail, with the docstring text that contradicts them, and don't hide the problem.

Worth keeping: negating the result when `end < start` and starting at `start + ONE_DAY` both look consistent with the docstring. Please remove the `include_end` month/year logic and list any conflicting tests in the PR description.
